subject_line: Avoid quadratic accumulation when parsing long SQL expression lists (#963)
s1_reason: grammar.ne: free_form_sql:* replaced by a persistent linked list (expression_list); Nearley array concatenation copied every shared prefix, making long expression lists quadratic in time and memory
s2_reason: cost grows with the number of free_form_sql items in a clause/parenthesis (select list length, IN-list length, OR-chain length)
s3_reason: grammar <select_list> ::= <target_el> <more_target_el>* (long select list = the #840 repro), <expr_list>/<more_expr>* inside IN (...) via <pred_expr>/<in_expr>, and <or_expr> right recursion (OR chains) all grow unboundedly; every item becomes a free_form_sql node in select_clause/other_clause/parenthesis, i.e. the changed rules. Runner engine=formatter times fmt.format(sql,{language:postgresql}) = parse+format, so parse cost lands in runtime_ns; memory reduction lands in rss metrics.
confounds: Same range v15.8.2..v15.9.0 also has: #972 reserved word after AS treated as alias (lexer disambiguateTokens, can change parse/output when an alias is a reserved word); #959 BETWEEN output spacing (BETWEEN is in the grammar, output length differs by 1 char); #958 OPERATOR() spacing only with denseOperators (not set by runner); pg_dump restrict commands (postgresql.formatter.ts, not SELECT); #960 DuckDB and #971 SingleStoreDB (other dialects). None is a perf change; #972/#959 are small output changes, so formatted lengths differ for a few inputs.
notes: Deduplicated: branch commit e2ed5ec (2026-08-07, same diff, author arc-oai) merged as 6c21ff5; also listed under "Performance" in the v15.9.0 GitHub release notes. Both versions on npm; subjects/sql_formatter_latest already aliases 15.8.2 and 15.9.0. Output is identical by design (perf-only refactor). Also re-enables the memory test from eb187fe.
